title: Stability primer: tiered safeguards & quiet flip checklist
content:
Purpose
- Quick personal reference for rolling a model variant with minimal customer impact.
- Combine quiet traffic shifts + tiered safety gates + cache priming to avoid cold-token latency spikes.
- Keep this as a terse runbook for late-night flips (notes to self).

High-level approach (one-liner)
- Slow, measured cohort introduction (0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20%) over ~6 hours with automated signal checks and an immediate pinback path. Pre-warm KV caches for hot endpoints before increasing traffic.

Key assumptions
- New model is compatible with current tokenizer and prompt format.
- Metrics stream (prod-metrics) emits: latency_p50/p90/p99, error_rate, cost_per_token, token_throughput, top_upstream_429s, llm_quality_regressions (from eval harness).
- We have runtime fallback to previous quantized variant in same family.

Before flip (prep checklist)
- [ ] Confirm PR merge + image digest. (PR 934 image: gcr.io/rwinference/serving-runtime:sha256:abc123)
- [ ] Bake a canary infra image: run local warmup (see warmup commands).
- [ ] Tag release in infra and create release note stub (internal).
- [ ] Create canary cohort: label clients (cohort=canary-a) and set SDK flag.
- [ ] Prepare telemetry dashboard: show baseline (last 72h) for all metrics, and set alert thresholds.
- [ ] Run a short A/B offline eval against holdout prompt set -> record BLEU/ROUGE-ish and hallucination counts.
- [ ] Pick initial warmup keys and a script to pre-populate KV caches.
- [ ] Notify on-call SRE + product owner + key customer contacts. Post message in #deployments and #oncall.

Warmup plan (notes)
- Goal: bring KV caches and prefix caches to steady-state for the hot 80% of requests. Avoid p99 spikes caused by cache misses.
- Strategy: use a mixture of synthetic requests and captured production traces (anonymized).
- Command (dry-run):
  - ./tools/warmup --image gcr.io/rwinference/serving-runtime:sha256:abc123 --keys warmup-keys.json --concurrency 30 --duration 10m
- Hotkey selection: pick top 200 prefixes from last 24h (requests frequency); map to representative prompts in warmup-keys.json.
- Stagger warmup across regions: start in us-west-2, wait 5m, then eu-west-1 to avoid global resource spikes.

Cohort sizing and timing (proposal)
- Phase 0 (smoke): 0.1% traffic, 15m -> check basic health.
- Phase 1: 1% traffic, 45m -> validate latency p90 within +20% of baseline and error_rate < baseline + 0.2pp.
- Phase 2: 5% traffic, 90m -> begin to surface any quality regressions. Run eval slices in parallel.
- Phase 3: 20% traffic, 3h -> sustained checks, start priming more keys if steady.
- Phase 4: 50%+ if all good.
- Note: Each phase must pass automated checks and a manual green from on-call before proceeding.

Automated gating signals (hard thresholds)
- latency_p90 increase > 30% -> immediate rollback/scale-up decision.
- latency_p99 increase > 50% -> immediate rollback.
- error_rate > baseline + 0.5 percentage points -> rollback.
- downstream 429s spike > 3x baseline OR sustained for > 5m -> rollback.
- cost_per_token increase > 2x expected for the family -> require product sign-off.
- llm_quality_regressions: any new hallucination cluster > 2% on selected prompts -> hold and investigate.

Soft signals (contextual, require human judgment)
- small increase in p95 but stable p99 and no error rate rise -> consider continuing but monitor.
- slight decrease in throughput due to batching changes -> watch unit economics but don't rollback immediately.

Rollback and pinning playbook (fast path)
- Fast rollback trigger: alert fires on hard threshold OR manual pin request from PO/SRE.
- Actions:
  1) Flip routing rule in router-service to previous model variant (route override) -> expected propagation < 30s for route config.
  2) If route flip fails or is slow, set per-customer SDK pin to previous model for top 50 customers (scripted).
  3) Revert image in infra agent and mark canary as failed in release notes.
  4) Capture full traces and dump hot keys; attach to the incident ticket.
- Post-rollback: do a 1-hour observation window, then run a root-cause capture (RCA-notes template).

Manual pinning quick commands
- Pin via admin-console (UI) -> select tenant -> model-pin -> set to previous sha.
- CLI shortcut (internal): rwctl tenant pin --tenant-id T-12345 --model sha256:prev987
- SDK override: set RW_SDK_FORCE_MODEL=sha256:prev987 for targeted clients.

Observability checklist (live)
- [ ] Confirm metric stream shows canary cohort distinct tag (cohort=canary-a).
- [ ] Tracing: sample rate up for canary cohort x10 to catch pathologies.
- [ ] Error logs: attach request payloads for first 100 errors (redact PII).
- [ ] Latency heatmap: watch region-by-region for divergence.
- [ ] Cost dashboard: rolling 1h cost-per-token.
- [ ] Quality monitors: run auto-evals every 30m on the canary responses for core prompts.

Customer-facing considerations
- Avoid enabling canary for tenants on dedicated or lower SLAs unless explicitly approved.
- For key enterprise customers with strict SLOs, offer SDK toggle and pre-signed plan.
- Pre-draft email for product: brief note on what changed + pin instructions in case they see degradation.

Open questions / TODOs (personal)
- How to integrate KV warmup with autoscaler without overshooting GPU memory during warmup bursts? Need a safe concurrency schedule.
- Can we expose a "warmup-only" job that uses idle capacity windows? Talk to infra.
- Add a safety gate to automatically reduce batch size if p99 climbs during warmup.
- Investigate whether prefetching tokenizer caches yields measurable p99 improvement.

Post-mortem notes (template reminders)
- Timestamp when canary first flipped.
- First alert and which threshold.
- Action timeline (who did what at what time).
- Snapshot of metrics (pre/post) and traces.
- Root cause hypothesis and mitigation steps.
- Lessons learned / checklist updates.

Quick heuristics (rules of thumb I use)
- If p90 moves but p99 stays flat and errors low -> likely batching or distribution change, continue with caution.
- If latency spike coincides with increased 429s downstream -> capacity/backpressure issue, not model quality.
- Always give a 15m settle period after any routing change before making additional changes.

Last-minute checklist for late-night flips
- [ ] Slack ping to #oncall with exact time window.
- [ ] Confirm SRE and PO are awake/available.
- [ ] Run warmup in staging mirror first (10m).
- [ ] Take full heap/profile snapshot on one canary instance.
- [ ] Keep rollback CLI open and tested.

Notes-to-self (short):
- Don’t push beyond 5% if cold-start patterns show repeated p99 spikes.
- Keep manual pins easy: top customers should have prefilled pin scripts.
- Revisit warmup key generation every 2 weeks; traffic patterns drift fast.

Appendix: quick references
- Warmup script location: infra/tools/warmup
- Pin CLI help: ./rwctl --help tenant pin
- Incident ticket template: confluence/incident-templates/canary-rollback
- Eval harness: github.com/redwood-inference/evals/canary-suite

End of notes (save as unstable, will refine).
